The dialogue presents a clinical encounter with a patient presenting with subacute symptoms of shortness of breath, progressive abdominal distension (over 1 month), and fatigue—without peripheral edema, chest pain, cough, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Imaging reveals a large right ovarian mass and significant ascites. The absence of vaginal bleeding, menstrual changes, or gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g., early satiety, bloating) reduces—but does not eliminate—the likelihood of gynecologic malignancy or functional ovarian pathology. Ovarian malignancy with malignant ascites
